day.reading: fixation times applied to the Weasel give 540,000 generations, 10,800x Dawkins's 50

critic.reading: the Weasel is truncation selection on a known target (a different model, conceded in D9a q2); within Day's model the serial sum overstates the time

notes: Every printed figure reproduces from (2/s) ln(2N) and a serial sum over 27 letters: 396 and 19,807 per letter, 10,696 and 534,788 in total (Day rounds per letter first: 27 x 400 = 10,800 shown as 11,000, 27 x 20,000 = 540,000); 540,000/50 = 10,800, 10^4.03. Within Day's own model the per-letter sweep time is 2.3x the conditional mean (8,532 asymptote; 8,525 simulated) and letters at independent sites need not fix in series: the parallel maximum is about 13,100, 41x below 540,000 and still 262x Dawkins's 50. Which model describes the program is M-408, not this record.
